behavior_constraints: C3 changes the --run-id validator regex to ^[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+$ while still requiring non-empty values; empty, leading dot, trailing dot, exactly . or .., and any two-or-more consecutive dots exit 4 with invalid --run-id: <raw>.
Dotted but otherwise legal ids such as foo.bar, dA.1, and v1.2.3-rc.0 are accepted and used verbatim; generated default ids remain run-YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ-<6hex> with no dot.

The same run-id validator and edge checks apply to --run-id and prior-run-id positionals for flowr run, flowr run --resume, flowr replay, and flowr diff; malformed values exit 4 with invalid --run-id: <raw>.
For flowr diff, a malformed run-id error wins over the argument-count message when two args are supplied but one is malformed; the distinct-id error fires only on exact byte equality.
Resumed runs still require the new run id to differ byte-for-byte from the prior id; both ids may contain dots.
FLOWR_RUN_ID, run_started/run_resumed/run_finished events, and report.run_id carry the final run id verbatim, including dots, with no escaping or normalization; cache keys are unaffected.
Steps may declare a free-form tags: string list; tags are parsed, validated, and preserved through matrix/foreach expansion.
flowr run accepts CLI tag filtering; when a filter is supplied only matching steps execute, and with no filter all steps run as before.
Workflows may declare run-level budgets; execution tracks usage, enforces budget limits, and reports budget status/summary, with neutral values for older reports.

All R1-R6 validation rules, exit codes, scheduling, caching, interpolation, hooks, retries, when, foreach, outputs, secrets, artifacts, dry-run, graph, locks, diff, and lint behavior remains unchanged except the C3 acceptance of dotted run ids.
